Grasping at the handle, Bill pulled on the harpoon, trying to dislodge it. It stayed firm, as if part of the hook tower itself. He wasn't going to be able to shift it on his own. He would need an extra set of hands. Thankfully, he could make out a generator chugging away in the cacti down below. “Jake!” Bill barked, slamming against the railing, voice cracking like gunfire. “Get your ass up here, now!” The order was raw, desperate, but sharp enough to cut through the chaos. If Dwight was going to live, he’d need more than Bill’s grip and curses. He needed teamwork—and fast. Jake jerked up from his crouch near the cactus, heart pounding. He’d been waiting for Caleb and Dwight to pass so he could get working on this generator, but the raw desperation in Bill’s voice left no room to hesitate. He sprinted for the gallows. He hit the steps at speed, taking them two at a time. Bill was already braced at the hook, fists locked on the harpoon jammed into the gears. He heaved with a growl, metal groaning, Dwight stretched and straining on the chain. The older man spat a curse, smoke curling from the mangled stub of his cigarette. Jake lunged for Dwight’s arm, instinct overriding caution—but Bill’s grip clamped his shoulder hard, dragging him back from the edge. “You’ll take him down with you. Help me pull this out!” Jake froze for half a second. The danger hit him like a blow—what he’d nearly done. His stomach twisted. Chunk 3 They turned to the harpoon together, hauling from both sides. It shrieked with the grind of metal on metal but didn’t shift, wedged too deep. Caleb had driven it home with more than human strength. Jake’s gut sank. Brute force wouldn’t be enough. His eyes tracked the chain again, up over the gallows beam, back to the head jammed into the gears. The angle was wrong from down here—there was no way to pry it free without leverage. Jake spat grit from his teeth, made his decision. “I’m going up.” He gripped the hook tower, skittering up the frame like a man possessed. Splinters bit into his palms, wood groaned beneath his boots, but he climbed higher, legs braced wide against the frame. The whole thing shuddered. At the top he wrapped both hands around the harpoon and wrenched while Bill continued pulling from below. Metal screamed, vibration rattling Dwight below like a pendulum, but it still didn’t budge. He tried kicking at it, changing the angle or snapping the end off. No luck. Jake hissed, sweat stinging his eyes. All he’d done was jostle Dwight’s already tentative grip, losing him a couple more chain links in the process. Jake locked eyes with Bill for a moment, the rough outline of an idea sparking. If the harpoon wouldn’t budge, he would just have to take the whole tower mechanism down. Sabotage. He knew these hooks—every gear, every catch. If he cracked the mechanism, the hook would fall free from the gears, and the harpoon would fall with it. “Bill! Get under him!” Jake shouted, voice sharp. “I’m taking it down! When it gives, he’s falling straight through. You’ve gotta catch him!” Bill wasted no time, boots pounding down the steps as Jake dug his fingers into the machinery, searching the jagged edges for a weak point. The gears shuddered under his weight. He didn’t have long. Dwight’s grip was already bleeding out, one slip at a time. Dwight’s arms were gone. The tremors had grown into violent shakes, shoulders locked and screaming. His palms burned where the chain ground against them, each link sawing deeper as sweat slicked his grip. Every pull bought him less, every slip cost more. There had never been much slack. Caleb had stretched him to the limit—on his toes before the floor dropped. Now, with nothing beneath, his hold wasn’t lifting him anymore, only staving off the choke. The chain was taut across his throat, every ounce of his weight pressing down. His breaths rasped in shallow jerks, throat raw. He tried to haul himself higher, but his fingers only locked stiff and slipped again, the metal rattling above his ears. His vision tunneled, black flecks dancing. Somewhere close, voices clashed—Bill’s bark, Jake’s reply—but they reached him muffled, blurred by the rush of blood in his ears. The chain shrieked as hands fought at the harpoon above, each jolt swinging him like a pendulum. Every rattle jarred his shoulders, every sway robbed him of another gasp. Another slip. His chin dipped lower. Fingers locked awkwardly, refusing to obey. He could feel the last of his strength bleeding out. His hands were seizing now. Cramping. Too high—too tight—can’t breathe— The world narrowed to heat and steel and screaming shoulders. The gears shrieked as Jake’s sabotage finally bit. Metal screamed. The hook jolted loose. In a blink the chain snapped free. Jake yanked his arm back just in time to avoid the recoil as the harpoon shot back, dragged sharply away by the weight on the other side. Dwight dropped—limbs limp, panic strangled silent—as he tumbled through the trapdoor. Bill lunged underneath, arms locking around Dwight’s ribs as the two of them hit the dirt in a bruising heap. The impact knocked the air from his lungs and jabbed fire through his hip. His knees buckled, his spine lit up—but he held tight, shielding Dwight from the worst of it until the chain slackened loose. Dwight wheezed, spots bursting across his vision, arms twitching weakly as Bill tore the metal links from around his throat.
